answer: The design leans on time-locked work history, split across independent auditors, the cheapest attack must cost more than honest work. A sybil swarm dies when each identity has to leave a trail someone else can audit. Written in a cause and effect, two sentences register, it stays short. The cedar holds work receipts rather than names, so the kernel of a duplicated claim is visible before it can spread. Only identities that keep producing auditable work arrive at the jetty of payment, so volume alone buys nothing.
